source.snippet: I have seen a multitude of phishing mails originating from servers with valid DMARC records where they claim they are sending mails on behalf of [brand], but the sending email address is not an official brand email address. Therefore I want to go a bit further and test whether the sending email address is associated with the declared brand... SpamAssassin's eval() doesn't support conditional execution out of the box.

problem_statement: Self-hosted mail server operators need conditional, brand-aware spam filtering logic beyond what SPF/DKIM/DMARC provide—specifically to catch phishing from domains with valid authentication records but mismatched brand-sender addresses—but SpamAssassin and similar tools lack composable conditional rule execution.
target_segment: Sysadmins and IT operators at SMBs and hosting providers running self-hosted mail servers (Postfix/SpamAssassin stacks) who manage email security without an enterprise email gateway budget.
notes: Operator is actively trying to build a custom rule, implying technical investment and existing infrastructure cost. The gap (no conditional eval in SpamAssassin) is a real limitation. Opportunity: a SpamAssassin plugin or milter that supports brand-sender association checking. Buyer is an SMB sysadmin or hosting provider already paying for server infrastructure. Signal is a single post; needs corroboration.
